newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish debt ended sharply higher in a listless session on Monday, matching foreign market gains at the opening and then trading sideways, dealers said.

"It's very quiet here, with London on holiday," a dealer in Madrid said. But others added the market was also lacking fuel to increase initial gains because Treasury auctions were suggesting a more cautious approach to traders.
On Tuesday and Wednesday, the Treasury will sell three-, five-, 10-, and 15-year bonds for an expected 375 billion pesetas. "The underlying trend is still very positive," a dealer said.
"Later in the week, after the auction, I'd expect the market to jump ahead," a dealer added.
Traders expect April CPI to show a yearly rate below 2.0 percent, down from 2.2 percent in March. Such a drop would boost fresh expectations of another cut in the key money market.
CPI is scheduled for release on May 14.
But other dealers in Madrid said the 10-year spread over Bunds rounding the level of 100 basis points was offering a fair value. They were ruling out bigger movement in bonos near term.
